title.zh: 卷七十一 列傳第三十一 徐湛 江湛 王僧綽
title.en: Volume 71 Biographies 31: Xu Zhan, Jiang Zhan, Wang Sengchao
title.raw: 卷七十一 列傳第三十一 徐湛 江湛 王僧綽 Volume 71 Biographies 31: Xu Zhan, Jiang Zhan, Wang Sengchao

sentences.zh: 列傳第三十一 徐湛之江湛王僧綽

translations.literal: Biographies 31: Xu Zhanzhi, Jiang Zhan, and Wang Sengchuo
translations.idiomatic: Biography 31: Xu Zhanzhi, Jiang Zhan, and Wang Sengchuo

sentences.zh: 徐湛之，字孝源，東海郯人。

translations.literal: Xu Zhanzhi, style name Xiaoyuan, was a native of Tan in Donghai commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zhanzhi, styled Xiaoyuan, came from Tan in Donghai commandery.

sentences.zh: 司徒羨之兄孫，吳郡太守佩之弟子也。

translations.literal: He was a grandson of the elder brother of Minister over the Masses Xianzhi and a nephew of Peizhi, Governor of Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was a grandson of Minister over the Masses Xianzhi's elder brother and a nephew of Wu commandery Governor Peizhi.

sentences.zh: 祖欽之，秘書監。

translations.literal: His grandfather Qinzhi was Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Qinzhi had served as Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 父逵之，尚高祖長女會稽公主，為振威將軍、彭城、沛二郡太守。

translations.literal: His father Kuizhi married Princess Kuaiji, the eldest daughter of Gaozu, and served as General Who Quells Might and Governor of the two commanderies of Pengcheng and Pei.
translations.idiomatic: His father Kuizhi had married Princess Kuaiji, Gaozu's eldest daughter, and held the posts of General Who Quells Might and governor of Pengcheng and Pei commanderies.

sentences.zh: 高祖諸子並幼，以逵之姻戚，將大任之，欲先令立功。

translations.literal: Gaozu's sons were all still young; because Kuizhi was a kinsman by marriage, he was to be given a great charge and was first to be made to win merit.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu's sons were still young; as a kinsman by marriage, Kuizhi was marked for high office, but first he was to earn distinction in the field.

sentences.zh: 及討司馬休之，使統軍為前鋒，配以精兵利器，事克，當即授荊州。

translations.literal: When he campaigned against Sima Xiuzhi, Kuizhi was made to command the army as vanguard, furnished with picked troops and sharp weapons; once the affair succeeded, he was at once to be given Jing province.
translations.idiomatic: In the campaign against Sima Xiuzhi he was placed at the head of the army as vanguard with elite troops and the best arms; on victory he was to receive Jing province immediately.

sentences.zh: 休之遣魯宗之子軌擊破之，於陣見害。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi sent Zongzi Gui of Lu to strike and break him; he was killed in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi sent Gui, son of Lu Zong, who routed him and killed him on the field.

sentences.zh: 追贈中書侍郎。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given the title of Vice Director of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Vice Director of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 湛之幼孤，為高祖所愛，常與江夏王義恭寢食不離於側。

translations.literal: Zhanzhi was orphaned young and was loved by Gaozu; he constantly slept and ate beside Prince Yigong of Jiangxia without leaving his side.
translations.idiomatic: Zhanzhi lost his father early and was cherished by Gaozu, who kept him at the side of Prince Yigong of Jiangxia day and night.

sentences.zh: 永初三年，詔曰：「永興公主一門嫡長，早罹辛苦。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongchu an edict said: "Princess Yongxing is the eldest legitimate child of her house and early suffered hardship.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yongchu an edict declared: "Princess Yongxing, eldest in her line, has known hardship from an early age.

sentences.zh: 外孫湛之，特所鍾愛。

translations.literal: Her grandson Zhanzhi is especially cherished.
translations.idiomatic: Her grandson Zhanzhi is especially dear to us.

sentences.zh: 且致節之胤，情實兼常。

translations.literal: Moreover, as a descendant who has shown utmost integrity, his affection is truly beyond the ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, as one who has shown utmost integrity, his devotion is truly exceptional.

sentences.zh: 可封枝江縣侯，食邑五百戶。

translations.literal: He may be enfeoffed as Marquis of Zhijiang county with a fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Let him be enfeoffed as Marquis of Zhijiang with a fief of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 」年數歲，與弟淳之共車行，牛奔車壞，左右馳來赴之。

translations.literal: " When he was only a few years old, riding in a carriage with his younger brother Chunzhi, the ox bolted and the carriage broke; attendants galloped up to help.
translations.idiomatic: " While still a small boy, he was riding with his younger brother Chunzhi when the ox bolted and wrecked the carriage; attendants rushed to their aid.

sentences.zh: 湛之先令取弟，眾咸歎其幼而有識。

translations.literal: Zhanzhi first ordered them to take his brother; all sighed in admiration that even as a child he had such sense.
translations.idiomatic: Zhanzhi told them to rescue his brother first; everyone marveled that even as a child he showed such judgment.

sentences.zh: 及長，頗涉大義，善自位待。

translations.literal: When he grew up, he was well versed in great principles and knew how to comport himself in his station.
translations.idiomatic: As he matured he gained a solid grasp of moral principle and knew how to conduct himself according to his rank.

sentences.zh: 事祖母及母，並以孝謹聞。

translations.literal: In serving his grandmother and his mother, he was alike renowned for filial piety and dutiful care.
translations.idiomatic: His care of his grandmother and mother alike won him a reputation for filial devotion and reverence.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二年，除著作佐郎，員外散騎侍郎，並不就。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanjia he was appointed Assistant in the Bureau of Composition and Extraordinary Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, but accepted neither post.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yuanjia he was offered the posts of Assistant in the Bureau of Composition and Extraordinary Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, but declined both.

sentences.zh: 六年，東宮始建，起家補太子洗馬，轉國子博士，遷奮威將軍、南彭城、沛二郡太守，徙黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, when the Eastern Palace was first established, he began his career as Supplementer to the Crown Prince's Household as Groom of the Heir Apparent, became Erudite of the National University, was promoted to General Who Displays Might and Governor of the two commanderies of Nan Pengcheng and Pei, and was transferred to Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, when the heir apparent's establishment was founded, he entered service as Groom of the Heir Apparent, became Erudite of the National University, was promoted to General Who Displays Might and governor of Nan Pengcheng and Pei, and then moved to Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 祖母年老，辭以朝直，不拜。

translations.literal: His grandmother was old; he declined on the ground of court duty and did not accept the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: His grandmother was elderly; citing his obligation to attend court, he declined the appointment.

sentences.zh: 復授二郡，加輔國將軍，遷秘書監，領右軍將軍，轉侍中，加驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: He was again given the two commanderies and made General Who Assists the State; he was moved to Director of the Secretariat, concurrently Right Army General, transferred to Palace Attendant, and given the additional title of Valiant Cavalry General.
translations.idiomatic: He was again given the two commanderies with the rank of General Who Assists the State, became Director of the Secretariat while holding the post of Right Army General, was made Palace Attendant, and received the additional title of Valiant Cavalry General.

sentences.zh: 復為秘書監，加散騎常侍，驍騎如故。

translations.literal: He again became Director of the Secretariat and was given the additional post of Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry; his valiant cavalry title remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: He again became Director of the Secretariat with the additional rank of Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, retaining his valiant cavalry title.

sentences.zh: 會稽公主身居長嫡，為太祖所禮，家事大小，必咨而後行。

translations.literal: Princess Kuaiji, as the eldest legitimate daughter, was honored by the Taizu; in household affairs great and small, he always consulted her before acting.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Kuaiji, as eldest legitimate daughter, was held in honor by Emperor Wen; on household matters great and small he always sought her counsel before acting.

sentences.zh: 西征謝晦，使公主留止台內，總攝六宮。

translations.literal: On the western campaign against Xie Hui, he had the princess remain within the terrace compound to oversee the six palaces in general.
translations.idiomatic: On the western campaign against Xie Hui he left the princess at court to oversee the inner palaces.

sentences.zh: 忽有不得意，輒號哭，上甚憚之。

translations.literal: Whenever she was suddenly displeased, she would wail aloud; the emperor greatly feared this.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever something displeased her she would burst into loud weeping, and the emperor was much afraid of it.

sentences.zh: 初，高祖微時，貧陋過甚，嘗自往新洲伐荻，有納布衫襖等衣，皆敬皇后手自作；

translations.literal: Earlier, when Gaozu was still obscure, he was exceedingly poor and mean; he once went himself to Xinzhou to cut reeds; there were garments such as a cotton jacket and padded coat, all made by the hand of Empress Jing herself;
translations.idiomatic: In his early days Gaozu had been desperately poor; he once went to Xinzhou himself to cut reeds. A cotton jacket and padded coat he owned had been sewn by Empress Jing with her own hands;

sentences.zh: 高祖既貴，以此衣付公主，曰：「後世若有驕奢不節者，可以此衣示之。

translations.literal: after Gaozu had risen to eminence, he gave these garments to the princess, saying, "If in later generations there is anyone arrogant, extravagant, and without restraint, you may show him these garments."
translations.idiomatic: after he rose to power he gave those garments to the princess, saying, "If any descendant grows arrogant and extravagant, show him these clothes."

sentences.zh: 」湛之為大將軍彭城王義康所愛，與劉湛等頗相附協。

translations.literal: Zhanzhi was loved by Grand General Prince Yikang of Pengcheng and was rather closely allied with Liu Tan and others.
translations.idiomatic: Zhanzhi won the favor of Grand General Yikang, Prince of Pengcheng, and aligned himself closely with Liu Tan and his circle.

sentences.zh: 及劉湛得罪，事連湛之，太祖大怒，將致大辟。

translations.literal: When Liu Tan was punished for his offense, the affair implicated Zhanzhi; the Taizu was greatly enraged and was about to impose the death penalty.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Tan fell, the case implicated Zhanzhi; Emperor Wen was furious and was about to sentence him to death.

sentences.zh: 湛之憂懼無計，以告公主。

translations.literal: Zhanzhi, anxious and at his wits' end, told the princess.
translations.idiomatic: In dread and despair Zhanzhi confided in the princess.

sentences.zh: 公主即日入宮，既見太祖，因號哭下床，不復施臣妾之禮。

translations.literal: That very day the princess entered the palace; once she had seen the Taizu, she wailed and threw herself from the couch, no longer observing the rites due from a subject or consort.
translations.idiomatic: The princess went to court that same day; as soon as she saw Emperor Wen she wailed and threw herself from the couch, abandoning all courtly decorum.

sentences.zh: 以錦囊盛高祖納衣，擲地以示上曰：「汝家本貧賤，此是我母為汝父作此納衣。

translations.literal: She placed Gaozu's cotton garments in a brocade pouch and flung them to the ground to show the emperor, saying, "Your house was originally poor and base; this is the cotton garment my mother made for your father."
translations.idiomatic: She took Gaozu's cotton garments from a brocade pouch and flung them down before the emperor. "Your family was poor," she cried. "My mother sewed this cotton coat for your father."

sentences.zh: 今日有一頓飽食，便欲殘害我兒子！

translations.literal: Now that you have one full meal, you wish to destroy my son!"
translations.idiomatic: Now that you have your fill, you would destroy my son!"

sentences.zh: 」上亦號哭，湛之由此得全也。

translations.literal: The emperor also wailed aloud, and by this means Zhanzhi was spared.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wept as well, and Zhanzhi was spared.

sentences.zh: 遷中護軍，未拜，又遷太子詹事，尋加侍中。

translations.literal: He was moved to Central Army Protector; before he took office he was again moved to Steward of the Heir Apparent's Household, and soon after was given the additional post of Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Central Army Protector but did not take up the post; he was then made Steward of the Heir Apparent's Household and soon after Palace Attendant as well.

sentences.zh: 湛之善於尺牘，音辭流暢。

translations.literal: Zhanzhi was skilled at letters and his words flowed with ease.
translations.idiomatic: Zhanzhi wrote with great skill, his phrasing fluent and graceful.

sentences.zh: 貴戚豪家，產業甚厚。

translations.literal: As a noble kinsman of a great house, his estates were very substantial.
translations.idiomatic: As a great noble house, his wealth was immense.

sentences.zh: 室宇園池，貴游莫及。

translations.literal: His halls, gardens, and ponds no noble visitor could match.
translations.idiomatic: His mansions, gardens, and ponds surpassed those of any noble in the capital.

sentences.zh: 伎樂之妙，冠絕一時。

translations.literal: The excellence of his performers and music crowned the age.
translations.idiomatic: His musicians and entertainers were unrivaled in their day.

sentences.zh: 門生千餘人，皆三吳富人之子，姿質端妍，衣服鮮麗。

translations.literal: His retainers numbered more than a thousand, all sons of wealthy men of the Three Wu regions, of fine bearing and handsome dress.
translations.idiomatic: He kept more than a thousand retainers, all sons of wealthy families from the Three Wu, handsome in face and splendid in dress.

sentences.zh: 每出入行遊，途巷盈滿，泥雨日，悉以後車載之。

translations.literal: Whenever he went out on pleasure excursions, the streets and lanes were filled to overflowing; on muddy rainy days they were all carried in follow-up carriages.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he went abroad the streets were packed with his train; on muddy days they rode in carriages at the rear of the procession.

sentences.zh: 太祖嫌其侈縱，每以為言。

translations.literal: The Taizu disliked his extravagance and license and often spoke of it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen disapproved of his extravagance and often reproved him for it.

sentences.zh: 時安成公何勖，無忌之子也，臨汝公孟靈休，昶之子也，並各奢豪，與湛之共以肴膳、器服、車馬相尚。

translations.literal: At the time Duke of Ancheng He Xu, son of Wuji, and Duke of Linru Meng Lingxiu, son of Chang, were each likewise extravagant; with Zhanzhi they vied in delicacies, vessels and dress, and carriages and horses.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Xu of Ancheng, son of Wuji, and Duke Lingxiu of Linru, son of Chang, were equally lavish; with Zhanzhi they competed in cuisine, furnishings, dress, and equipage.

sentences.zh: 京邑為之語曰：「安成食，臨汝飾。

translations.literal: The capital had a saying about them: "Ancheng for food, Linru for adornment."
translations.idiomatic: The capital had a saying: "Ancheng for food, Linru for finery."

sentences.zh: 」湛之二事之美，兼于何、孟。

translations.literal: Zhanzhi excelled in both pursuits and surpassed He and Meng together.
translations.idiomatic: Zhanzhi surpassed them both in food and finery alike.

sentences.zh: 勖官至侍中，追諡荒公。

translations.literal: Xu rose to Palace Attendant and was posthumously given the temple name Duke of Dissipation.
translations.idiomatic: Xu reached the post of Palace Attendant and was posthumously styled Duke of Dissipation.

sentences.zh: 靈休善彈棋，官至秘書監。

translations.literal: Lingxiu was skilled at pitch-pot chess and rose to Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Lingxiu was a master of pitch-pot and rose to Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 湛之遷冠軍將軍、丹陽尹，進號征虜將軍，加散騎常侍，以公主憂不拜。

translations.literal: Zhanzhi was moved to Champion General and Governor of Danyang, advanced in title to General Who Pacifies the Barbarians, and given the additional post of Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry; because of the princess's mourning he did not accept office.
translations.idiomatic: Zhanzhi was made Champion General and Governor of Danyang, promoted to General Who Pacifies the Barbarians with the additional rank of Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, but declined the posts while the princess was in mourning.

sentences.zh: 過葬，復授前職，湛之表啟固辭，又詣廷尉受罪；

translations.literal: After the burial period he was again given his former posts; Zhanzhi memorialized firmly declining and also went to the Minister of Justice to submit to punishment;
translations.idiomatic: After the mourning period he was offered his former posts again; Zhanzhi memorialized a firm refusal and presented himself to the Minister of Justice to accept punishment;

sentences.zh: 上詔獄官勿得受，然後就命。

translations.literal: the emperor ordered the prison officials not to receive him, and only then did he take up his commission.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor ordered the prison officials not to accept his submission, and only then did he take office.

sentences.zh: 固辭常侍，許之。

translations.literal: He firmly declined the regular attendant post and was permitted to do so.
translations.idiomatic: He firmly declined the attendant post, and his request was granted.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，范曄等謀逆，湛之始與之同，後發其事，所陳多不盡，為曄等款辭所連，乃詣廷尉歸罪，上慰遣令還郡。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, Fan Ye and others plotted rebellion; Zhanzhi had at first been party to them, but later exposed the affair; what he reported was largely incomplete, and he was implicated by the confessions of Ye and the rest; he then went to the Minister of Justice to acknowledge guilt; the emperor comforted him and sent him back to his commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year Fan Ye and others plotted treason. Zhanzhi had initially been involved but later exposed the plot; his report was incomplete, and Fan Ye's confessions implicated him further. He went to the Minister of Justice to confess; the emperor consoled him and sent him back to his post.

sentences.zh: 湛之上表曰：

translations.literal: Zhanzhi submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Zhanzhi submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 賊臣范曄、孔熙先等，連結謀逆，法靜尼宣分往還，與大將軍臣義康共相脣齒，備于鞠對。

translations.literal: The traitorous ministers Fan Ye, Kong Xixian, and others banded together in treason; the nun Fajing and Xuanfen went back and forth as messengers; with my lord Grand General Yikang they were lip and teeth to one another—the full account is set forth in the interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: The traitors Fan Ye, Kong Xixian, and their confederates plotted rebellion; the nun Fajing and Xuanfen carried messages between them; they were bound to Grand General Yikang like lip and teeth—the record of interrogation sets this forth in full.

sentences.zh: 伏尋仲承祖始達熙先等意，便極言奸狀。

translations.literal: I reflect that when Zhong Chengzu first conveyed the intentions of Xixian and the rest, he spoke at once in the utmost detail of their treacherous conduct.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhong Chengzu first relayed Xixian's designs, he spoke at once in full detail of their treachery.

sentences.zh: 而臣兒女近情，不識大體，上聞之初，不務指斥，紙翰所載，尤復漫略者，實以凶計既表，逆事歸露；

translations.literal: but I, in the partial affection of a parent, failed to grasp the larger issue; when I first reported to Your Majesty I did not press to denounce them, and what my written report contained was especially cursory—this was truly because the wicked plot had already been exposed and the treasonous affair had come to light;
translations.idiomatic: But I, swayed by family feeling, failed to grasp the larger issue; in my first report to Your Majesty I did not press the accusation, and my written memorial was especially vague—because the wicked plot was already exposed and treason had come to light;

sentences.zh: 又仰緣聖慈，不欲窮盡，故言勢依違，未敢縷陳。

translations.literal: furthermore, relying on Your sacred compassion, I did not wish to pursue matters to the end; therefore my words were hesitant and evasive, and I did not dare set forth every detail.
translations.idiomatic: and relying on Your compassion, I did not wish to pursue the matter to the end; hence my words were hesitant and I did not dare lay out every detail.

sentences.zh: 情旨無隱，已昭天鑒。

translations.literal: My true intent, without concealment, has already been clear to Heaven's scrutiny.
translations.idiomatic: My true intent, without concealment, is already clear to Heaven's scrutiny.

sentences.zh: 及群凶收禽，各有所列，曄等口辭，多見誣謗；

translations.literal: When the band of villains was seized, each made his own deposition; in the oral statements of Ye and the rest, I was much slandered;
translations.idiomatic: When the conspirators were seized each made his deposition; Fan Ye and the others, in their statements, slandered me heavily;

sentences.zh: 承祖醜言，紛紜特甚。

translations.literal: Chengzu's vile words were especially numerous and confused.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzu's calumnies were especially numerous.

sentences.zh: 乃雲臣與義康宿有密契，在省之言，期以為定，潛通姦意，報示天文。

translations.literal: They said that I had long held a secret pact with Yikang, that words spoken in the Secretariat were taken as fixed agreements, that I secretly communicated treacherous intent, and reported omens from the heavens.
translations.idiomatic: They claimed I had long held a secret pact with Yikang, that remarks in the Secretariat were taken as binding agreements, that I secretly communicated treasonous designs, and reported celestial omens to him.

sentences.zh: 末雲熙先縣指必同，以誑於曄，或以智勇見稱，或以愚懦為目。

translations.literal: Finally they said that Xixian, pointing to me, declared we would surely act together, to deceive Ye; sometimes I was praised as wise and brave, sometimes marked as foolish and timid.
translations.idiomatic: Finally they said Xixian, pointing at me, declared we would surely act together—to deceive Fan Ye; sometimes I was praised as wise and brave, sometimes dismissed as foolish and timid.

sentences.zh: 既美其信懷可履，復駭其動止必啟。

translations.literal: They praised my trustworthiness as something to be relied on, yet also alarmed themselves that my every move would surely reveal the plot.
translations.idiomatic: They praised my trustworthiness as reliable, yet feared that my every move would expose the plot.

sentences.zh: 凡諸詭妄，還自違伐，多舉事端，不究源統，齎傳之信，無有主名，所征之人，又已死沒，首尾乖互，自為矛楯。

translations.literal: All such deceptions refuted themselves; they raised many incidents without tracing them to their source; letters they carried had no named author; persons they cited were already dead; beginning and end contradicted each other—they were their own spears and shields.
translations.idiomatic: All such fabrications contradicted themselves; they cited many incidents without tracing their source; the letters they mentioned had no identifiable author; the persons they named were already dead; beginning and end conflicted—they refuted their own claims.

sentences.zh: 即臣誘引之辭，以為始謀之證，銜臣糾告，並見怨咎，縱肆狂言，必規禍陷。

translations.literal: They took my words of enticement as proof of initial plotting; they bore resentment at my denunciation and all showed malice; they let loose wild speech, surely aiming to bring disaster upon me.
translations.idiomatic: They twisted my words of persuasion into proof of initial plotting; resenting my denunciation, they all sought revenge with reckless accusations meant to destroy me.

sentences.zh: 伏自探省，亦復有由。

translations.literal: I reflect upon myself and find that there is indeed some cause for this.
translations.idiomatic: On reflection, I find there is indeed some cause for their accusations.

sentences.zh: 昔義康南出之始，敕臣入相伴慰，晨夕覲對，經逾旬日。

translations.literal: When Yikang was first sent south into exile, I was ordered to enter and keep him company in consolation; morning and evening I attended him in audience for more than ten days.
translations.idiomatic: When Yikang was first sent into exile in the south, I was ordered to keep him company and console him; morning and evening I was in his presence for more than ten days.

sentences.zh: 逆圖成謀，雖無顯然，懟容異意，頗形言旨。

translations.literal: Though the treasonous design and completed plot were not manifest, resentment showed in his bearing and alien intent appeared rather clearly in his words.
translations.idiomatic: Though no open treason appeared, resentment showed in his bearing and disaffection was evident in his words.

sentences.zh: 遺臣利刃，期以際會，臣苦相諫譬，深加拒塞。

translations.literal: He presented me with a sharp blade, expecting a moment of opportunity; I earnestly admonished and remonstrated with him, but he deeply rejected and blocked me.
translations.idiomatic: He gave me a sharp blade, awaiting the right moment; I earnestly remonstrated with him, but he firmly refused to listen.

sentences.zh: 以為怨憤所至，不足為慮，便以關啟，懼成虛妄，思量反覆，實經愚心，非為納受，曲相蔽匿。

translations.literal: I thought it sprang only from resentment and anger and was not worth concern; I intended to report it but feared it might prove empty and false; I turned the matter over in my mind again and again—this truly passed through my foolish heart; it was not that I accepted or connived, bending to conceal him.
translations.idiomatic: I thought it arose only from resentment and was not worth troubling Your Majesty with; I meant to report it but feared it might prove groundless; I weighed the matter again and again in my foolish mind—it was not that I accepted his plot or deliberately concealed him.

sentences.zh: 又令申情范曄，釋中間之憾，致懷蕭思話，恨婚意未申，謂此僥倖，亦不宣達。

translations.literal: He also had me convey his feelings to Fan Ye to release the grievance between them, and express regard for Xiao Sihua, regretting that the marriage proposal had not been carried through; I regarded this as a mere chance matter and likewise did not report it.
translations.idiomatic: He also had me convey his feelings to Fan Ye to settle their quarrel and express regard for Xiao Sihua, regretting that a marriage alliance had not been concluded; I regarded this as trivial and did not report it either.

sentences.zh: 陛下敦惜天倫，彰于四海，籓禁優簡，親理咸通；

translations.literal: Your Majesty cherishes family bonds and makes this manifest throughout the realm; princes in confinement receive generous and easy treatment, and kinship ties are all kept open;
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty cherishes family bonds and makes this known throughout the realm; princes in confinement are treated generously, and kinship ties remain open;

sentences.zh: 又昔蒙眷顧，不容自絕，音翰信命，時相往來。

translations.literal: moreover, having once received your gracious regard, I could not cut myself off; letters and messages passed between us from time to time.
translations.idiomatic: moreover, having once enjoyed your gracious favor toward him, I could not break off relations; letters and messages passed between us from time to time.

sentences.zh: 或言少意多，旨深文淺，辭色之間，往往難測。

translations.literal: Sometimes his words were few but his meaning great, the purport deep and the text shallow; in tone and expression they were often hard to fathom.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes his words were few but his meaning weighty, the purport deep though the text slight; his tone and expression were often hard to read.

sentences.zh: 臣每懼異聞，皆略而不答。

translations.literal: I always feared suspicious reports and answered only briefly or not at all.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing suspicious reports, I always answered briefly or not at all.

sentences.zh: 惟心無邪悖，故不稍以自嫌。

translations.literal: Only because my heart harbored no treachery did I not feel the least self-reproach.
translations.idiomatic: Only because my heart was free of treachery did I feel no need for self-reproach.

sentences.zh: 慺慺丹實，具如此啟。

translations.literal: With earnest sincerity and loyal truth, I report all as above.
translations.idiomatic: With earnest loyalty I report all of this to Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 至於法靜所傳，及熙先等謀，知實不早，見關之日，便即以聞。

translations.literal: As for what Fajing transmitted and the plots of Xixian and the rest, I did not learn the truth early; on the day I was implicated, I reported at once.
translations.idiomatic: As for Fajing's messages and the plots of Xixian and his confederates, I did not learn the truth early; on the day I was implicated I reported at once.

sentences.zh: 雖晨光幽燭，曲昭窮款，裁以正義，無所逃刑。

translations.literal: Though dawn light and hidden torch alike reveal the utmost truth, judged by righteousness there is no escaping punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Though Your Majesty's light reveals every detail of my confession, judged by justice I cannot escape punishment.

sentences.zh: 束骸北闕，請罪司寇，乾施含宥，未加治考，中旨頻降，制使還往，仰荷恩私，哀惶失守。

translations.literal: I bound my body at the northern gate and asked punishment from the Minister of Justice; Your gracious pardon withheld investigation; imperial orders came down repeatedly commanding me to return; I bear your private favor on high, grieving and fearful beyond composure.
translations.idiomatic: I presented myself at the northern gate to accept judgment from the Minister of Justice; Your gracious pardon spared me investigation; repeated imperial orders commanded my return; overwhelmed by your kindness, I am grief-stricken and distraught.

sentences.zh: 臣殃積罪深，丁罹酷罰，久應屏棄，永謝人理。

translations.literal: My accumulated guilt is deep; I have met with harsh punishment and long ought to have been cast aside, forever parted from human society.
translations.idiomatic: My accumulated guilt is deep; having suffered harsh punishment I ought long ago to have been cast aside, forever cut off from human society.

sentences.zh: 況奸謀所染，忠孝頓闕，智防愚淺，暗於禍萌，士類未明其心，群庶謂之同惡，朝野側目，眾議沸騰，專信仇隙之辭，不復稍相申體。

translations.literal: Moreover, stained by treacherous plotting, loyalty and filial piety are suddenly lacking; my wisdom guards poorly and my folly is shallow; I was blind to the sprouting of disaster; gentlemen do not understand my heart; the multitude calls me a fellow villain; court and countryside look askance; public talk boils over; they trust only words born of enmity and will not hear the least explanation.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, implicated in treason, I seem to have abandoned loyalty and filial piety; my wit is poor and my folly deep; I was blind to disaster in the making; the gentry do not understand my heart; the people call me a fellow conspirator; court and countryside look on with suspicion; public opinion seethes; they heed only the words of enemies and will hear no explanation.

sentences.zh: 臣雖駑下，情非木石。

translations.literal: Though I am base and inferior, my feelings are not those of wood or stone.
translations.idiomatic: Though I am base and unworthy, I am not made of wood or stone.

sentences.zh: 豈不知醜點難嬰，伏劍為易。

translations.literal: How could I not know that shame is hard to bear and that falling on one's sword would be easy?
translations.idiomatic: Do I not know that shame is unbearable and that death by the sword would be easy?

sentences.zh: 而靦然視息，忍此餘生，實非苟吝微命，假延漏刻。

translations.literal: Yet I calmly draw breath and endure this remnant of life—not truly from grudging my slight existence or borrowing a few more moments.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I calmly draw breath and endure this remnant of life—not from clinging to a worthless existence or begging for a few more moments.

sentences.zh: 誠以負戾灰滅，貽惡方來，貪及視息，少自披訴；

translations.literal: It is truly because, bearing guilt that should turn to ashes, I would leave evil for the future; clinging to breath, I wish briefly to lay open my plea;
translations.idiomatic: It is truly because, bearing guilt that should reduce me to ashes, I would leave evil for posterity; clinging to life, I wish briefly to plead my case;

sentences.zh: 冀幽誠丹款，儻或昭然，雖復身膏草土，九泉無恨。

translations.literal: hoping that my hidden sincerity and loyal truth may perhaps become clear; though my body be grease for grass and soil, in the nine springs I would have no regret.
translations.idiomatic: hoping that my hidden sincerity may yet become clear; though my body nourish grass and soil, I would have no regret in the grave.

sentences.zh: 顯居官次，垢穢朝班，厚顏何地，可以自處。

translations.literal: To hold office openly defiles the court ranks; with what face can I place myself among them?
translations.idiomatic: To hold office openly defiles the court; with what face can I remain among its ranks?

sentences.zh: 乞蒙隳放，伏待鈇钅質。

translations.literal: I beg to be cast down and released, prostrate awaiting the axe.
translations.idiomatic: I beg to be dismissed and cast down, prostrate awaiting the executioner's axe.

sentences.zh: 上優詔不許。

translations.literal: The emperor issued a gracious edict and did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued a gracious edict refusing his request.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，服闋，轉中書令，領太子詹事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, when mourning was complete, he was transferred to Director of the Central Secretariat and concurrently Steward of the Heir Apparent's Household.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year, when his mourning was complete, he became Director of the Central Secretariat while retaining the post of Steward of the Heir Apparent's Household.

sentences.zh: 出為前軍將軍、南兗州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out as Forward Army General and Governor of Southern Yan province.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Forward Army General and Governor of Southern Yan province.

sentences.zh: 善於為政，威惠並行。

translations.literal: He was skilled in government, combining authority and kindness.
translations.idiomatic: He governed well, combining stern authority with kindness.

sentences.zh: 廣陵城舊有高樓，湛之更加修整，南望鐘山。

translations.literal: Guangling city had long had a high tower; Zhanzhi further restored and adorned it, facing south toward Zhong Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Guangling already had a tall tower; Zhanzhi restored and embellished it to look south toward Zhong Mountain.

sentences.zh: 城北有陂澤，水物豐盛。

translations.literal: North of the city were ponds and marshes, rich in aquatic creatures.
translations.idiomatic: North of the city lay ponds and marshes teeming with fish and waterfowl.

sentences.zh: 湛之更起風亭、月觀，吹台、琴室，果竹繁茂，花藥成行，招集文士，盡遊玩之適，一時之盛也。

translations.literal: Zhanzhi further raised the Wind Pavilion and Moon View, the Flute Terrace and Zither Room; fruit trees and bamboo grew luxuriantly, flowers and herbs stood in rows; he gathered literary men and enjoyed every pleasure of diversion—it was the splendor of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Zhanzhi added the Wind Pavilion and Moon View, the Flute Terrace and Zither Room; fruit trees and bamboo flourished, flowers and herbs lined the paths; he gathered literati and enjoyed every diversion—the glory of the age.

sentences.zh: 時有沙門釋惠休，善屬文，辭采綺豔，湛之與之甚厚。

translations.literal: At the time there was the monk Shi Huixiu, skilled at composition, his diction gorgeous and brilliant; Zhanzhi was very close to him.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the monk Huixiu was skilled at composition, his style gorgeous and brilliant; Zhanzhi was very close to him.

sentences.zh: 世祖命使還俗。

translations.literal: The Shizu ordered him to return to lay life.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu ordered him to return to lay life.

sentences.zh: 本姓湯，位至揚州從事史。

translations.literal: His original surname was Tang; he rose to Staff Officer of Yang province.
translations.idiomatic: His original surname was Tang; he rose to staff officer of Yang province.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，復入為丹陽尹，領太子詹事，將軍如故。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he again entered the capital as Governor of Danyang, concurrently Steward of the Heir Apparent's Household; his generalship remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year he returned to the capital as Governor of Danyang while retaining the post of Steward of the Heir Apparent's Household; his general's rank was unchanged.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，索虜至瓜步，湛之領兵置佐，與皇太子分守石頭。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year the northern barbarians reached Guabu; Zhanzhi led troops and set up his staff, sharing with the crown prince the defense of Shitou.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year the Northern Wei reached Guabu; Zhanzhi took command and, with the crown prince, jointly defended Shitou fortress.

sentences.zh: 二十八年春，魯爽兄弟率部曲歸順，爽等，魯軌子也。

translations.literal: In the spring of the twenty-eighth year, Lu Shuang and his brothers led their followers in submission; Shuang and the rest were sons of Lu Gui.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the twenty-eighth year Lu Shuang and his brothers led their followers in submission to the Song; they were sons of Lu Gui.

sentences.zh: 湛之以為廟算遠圖，特所獎納，不敢苟申私怨。

translations.literal: Zhanzhi regarded this as the court's far-reaching design and specially commended and accepted them; he did not dare lightly press a private grievance.
translations.idiomatic: Zhanzhi regarded their submission as part of the court's long-range strategy and warmly welcomed them, not daring to press a private grudge.

sentences.zh: 乞屏居田里，不許。

translations.literal: He begged to withdraw and live in the countryside; permission was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to retire to the countryside; his request was refused.

sentences.zh: 轉尚書僕射，領護軍將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and concurrently Army Protector General.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and concurrently Army Protector General.

sentences.zh: 時尚書令何尚之以湛之國戚，任遇隆重，欲以朝政推之。

translations.literal: At the time Director of the Masters of Writing He Shangzhi, because Zhanzhi was a kinsman of the imperial house and enjoyed weighty favor, wished to turn court affairs over to him.
translations.idiomatic: Director He Shangzhi, seeing that Zhanzhi was an imperial kinsman in high favor, wished to turn court affairs over to him.

sentences.zh: 凡諸辭訴，一不料省。

translations.literal: All petitions and suits he examined not at all.
translations.idiomatic: He examined none of the petitions and suits submitted.

sentences.zh: 湛之亦以《職官記》及令文，尚書令敷奏出內，事無不總，令缺則僕射總任。

translations.literal: Zhanzhi likewise cited the Record of Offices and the ordinance texts: the Director of the Masters of Writing presents memorials from within the palace and has general charge of all affairs; when the directorate is vacant the vice director assumes overall responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: Zhanzhi cited the Record of Offices and current regulations: the director presents memorials from within the palace and oversees all affairs; when that post is vacant the vice director assumes full responsibility.

sentences.zh: 又以事歸尚之，互相推委。

translations.literal: He also held that affairs belonged to Shangzhi; each pushed responsibility onto the other.
translations.idiomatic: He likewise held that affairs were Shangzhi's responsibility; the two pushed duty back and forth.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞袁淑並奏免官，詔曰：「令僕治務所寄，不共求體當，而互相推委，糾之是也。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Yuan Shu memorialized to dismiss them both from office; an edict said: "The director and vice director are entrusted with governing affairs; instead of jointly seeking what is fitting, they push responsibility onto each other—censure of them is right."
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Yuan Shu memorialized for their dismissal; an edict declared: "Director and vice director are entrusted with governing affairs; instead of working together they shirk responsibility—censure is justified."

sentences.zh: 然故事殘舛，所以致茲疑執，特無所問，時詳正之。

translations.literal: Yet precedent is fragmentary and confused, which gave rise to this dispute; they are specially not questioned, but the matter is to be clarified in due course.
translations.idiomatic: Yet precedent is fragmentary and confused, which caused this dispute; they are not punished for now, but the regulations are to be clarified.

sentences.zh: 」乃使湛之與尚之並受辭訴。

translations.literal: Zhanzhi and Shangzhi were then both made to receive petitions and suits.
translations.idiomatic: Zhanzhi and Shangzhi were then both ordered to handle petitions and suits.

sentences.zh: 尚之雖為令，而朝事悉歸湛之。

translations.literal: Although Shangzhi was director, court affairs all passed to Zhanzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Though Shangzhi held the directorship, all court affairs passed to Zhanzhi.

sentences.zh: 初，劉湛伏誅，殷景仁卒，太祖委任沈演之、庾炳之、范曄等，後又有江湛、何瑀之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Liu Tan was executed, Yin Jingren died, and the Taizu entrusted Shen Yanzhi, Yu Bingzhi, Fan Ye, and others; later there were also Jiang Zhan and He Yuzhi.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Tan was executed and Yin Jingren died, Emperor Wen entrusted Shen Yanzhi, Yu Bingzhi, Fan Ye, and others; later Jiang Zhan and He Yuzhi joined them.

sentences.zh: 曄誅，炳之免，演之、瑀之並卒，至是江湛為吏部尚書，與湛之並居權要，世謂之江、徐焉。

translations.literal: When Ye was executed, Bingzhi was dismissed, and Yanzhi and Yuzhi both died; by this time Jiang Zhan was Director of the Ministry of Personnel and with Zhanzhi jointly held power; the age called them Jiang and Xu.
translations.idiomatic: After Fan Ye's execution and Yu Bingzhi's dismissal, and with the deaths of Yanzhi and Yuzhi, Jiang Zhan became Director of Personnel and shared power with Xu Zhanzhi; the age spoke of "Jiang and Xu."

sentences.zh: 上每有疾，湛之輒入侍醫藥。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor fell ill, Zhanzhi would enter to attend him with medicine.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor fell ill, Zhanzhi attended him with medicine.

sentences.zh: 二凶巫蠱事發，上欲廢劭，賜浚死。

translations.literal: When the witchcraft affair of the two villains broke open, the emperor wished to depose Shao and grant Jun death.
translations.idiomatic: When the witchcraft plot of the two princes was exposed, the emperor wished to depose Shao and order Jun to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 而世祖不見寵，故累出外蕃，不得停京輦。

translations.literal: The Shizu, however, was not favored and was repeatedly sent out to border principalities, unable to remain at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jun, however, was not favored and was repeatedly posted to distant principalities, unable to remain at court.

sentences.zh: 南平王鑠、建平王宏並為上所愛，而鑠妃即湛妹，勸上立之。

translations.literal: Prince Shuo of Nanping and Prince Hong of Jianping were both loved by the emperor; Shuo's consort was Zhanzhi's younger sister, and she urged the emperor to establish him.
translations.idiomatic: Princes Shuo of Nanping and Hong of Jianping were both favored by the emperor; Shuo's consort was Zhanzhi's sister and urged the emperor to name Shuo heir.

sentences.zh: 元嘉末，征鑠自壽陽入朝，既至，又失旨，欲立宏，嫌其非次，是以議久不決。

translations.literal: At the end of Yuanjia, Shuo was summoned from Shouyang to court; once he arrived he again fell from favor; the emperor wished to establish Hong but disliked his irregular order of birth; thus deliberation long went unresolved.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Yuanjia, Shuo was summoned from Shouyang to court; once he arrived he again displeased the emperor. The emperor wished to name Hong heir but hesitated over his birth order, and deliberation dragged on.

sentences.zh: 與湛之屏人共言論，或連日累夕。

translations.literal: With Zhanzhi he discussed matters behind screened attendants, sometimes for days on end through successive nights.
translations.idiomatic: He discussed the matter with Zhanzhi in private, sometimes for days and nights on end.

sentences.zh: 每夜常使湛之自秉燭，繞壁檢行，慮有竊聽者。

translations.literal: Each night he would have Zhanzhi himself hold the candle and walk around the walls inspecting, fearing eavesdroppers.
translations.idiomatic: Each night he had Zhanzhi carry a candle and patrol the walls, fearing eavesdroppers.

sentences.zh: 劭入弑之旦，其夕，上與湛之屏人語，至曉猶未滅燭。

translations.literal: On the morning when Shao entered to commit regicide, that very evening the emperor had been speaking with Zhanzhi behind screened attendants; until dawn the candles were still not extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: On the night before Shao murdered him, the emperor had been speaking with Zhanzhi in private until dawn, candles still burning.

sentences.zh: 湛之驚起趣北戶，未及開，見害。

translations.literal: Zhanzhi started up in alarm and rushed to the north door; before he could open it he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhanzhi sprang up in alarm and rushed to the north door; before he could open it he was slain.

sentences.zh: 時年四十四。

translations.literal: He was forty-four years old.
translations.idiomatic: He was forty-four.

sentences.zh: 世祖即位，追贈司空，加散騎常侍，本官如故，諡曰忠烈公。

translations.literal: When the Shizu took the throne, he was posthumously given the office of Minister of Works and the additional title of Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry; his former offices remained as before; his posthumous name was Duke of Loyal Valor.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu took the throne, Zhanzhi was posthumously made Minister of Works with the additional rank of Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry; his former titles were confirmed; he was posthumously styled Duke of Loyal Valor.

sentences.zh: 又詔曰：「徐湛之、江湛、王僧綽門戶荼酷，遺孤流寓，言念既往，感痛兼深。

translations.literal: Another edict said: "The houses of Xu Zhanzhi, Jiang Zhan, and Wang Sengchuo have suffered bitter cruelty; orphaned survivors wander in exile; speaking of what has passed, grief and pain are alike deep."
translations.idiomatic: Another edict declared: "The houses of Xu Zhanzhi, Jiang Zhan, and Wang Sengchuo have suffered bitter cruelty; orphaned survivors wander in exile; remembering what has passed fills us with deep grief."

sentences.zh: 可令歸居本宅，厚加恤賜。

translations.literal: They may be ordered to return and dwell in their original residences, with generous relief and gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Let them return to their family homes and receive generous relief and gifts.

sentences.zh: 」於是三家長給廩。

translations.literal: Thereupon the three families received long-term grain rations.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the three families received long-term grain stipends.

sentences.zh: 三子：聿之、謙之，為元凶所殺。

translations.literal: He had three sons: Yuzhi and Qianzhi were killed by the prime villain.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons: Yuzhi and Qianzhi were killed by Liu Shao.

sentences.zh: 恆之嗣侯，尚太祖第十五女南陽公主，蚤卒，無子。

translations.literal: Hengzhi succeeded to the marquisate and married Princess Nanyang, the fifteenth daughter of the Taizu; he died young without sons.
translations.idiomatic: Hengzhi inherited the marquisate and married Princess Nanyang, Emperor Wen's fifteenth daughter; he died young without issue.

sentences.zh: 聿之子孝嗣紹封，齊受禪，國除。

translations.literal: Yuzhi's son Xiaosi succeeded to the enfeoffment; when Qi received the abdication, the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Yuzhi's son Xiaosi inherited the title; when the Qi dynasty succeeded the Song, the fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 江湛，字徽淵，濟陽考城人，湘州刺史夷子也。

translations.literal: Jiang Zhan, style name Huiyuan, was a native of Kaocheng in Jiyang commandery and the son of Yi, Governor of Xiang province.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Zhan, styled Huiyuan, came from Kaocheng in Jiyang commandery and was the son of Xiang province Governor Yi.

sentences.zh: 居喪以孝聞。

translations.literal: In mourning he was renowned for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: His filial devotion during mourning was widely praised.

sentences.zh: 愛好文義，喜彈棋鼓琴，兼明算術。

translations.literal: He loved literary principles, delighted in pitch-pot chess and the zither, and was also skilled in calculation.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning and letters, enjoyed pitch-pot and the zither, and was skilled in mathematics.

sentences.zh: 初為著作佐郎，遷彭城王義康司徒行參軍，南譙王義宣左軍功曹。

translations.literal: He first served as Assistant in the Bureau of Composition, was moved to Acting Staff Officer on Prince Yikang of Pengcheng's Secretariat as Minister over the Masses, and Recorder of the Left Army under Prince Yixuan of Nanqiao.
translations.idiomatic: He began as Assistant in the Bureau of Composition, then served on Prince Yikang of Pengcheng's staff and as recorder of the Left Army under Prince Yixuan of Nanqiao.

sentences.zh: 復為義康司徒主簿，太子中舍人。

translations.literal: He again served as Chief Clerk on Yikang's Secretariat as Minister over the Masses and as Household Attendant of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He again served as chief clerk on Yikang's secretariat and as attendant in the heir apparent's household.

sentences.zh: 司空檀道濟為子求湛妹婚，不許。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Tan Daoji sought Zhan's younger sister in marriage for his son; permission was refused.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Tan Daoji asked for Zhan's sister for his son; Zhan refused.

sentences.zh: 義康有命，又不從。

translations.literal: Yikang gave an order, and again he did not obey.
translations.idiomatic: Yikang commanded it, and again he refused.

sentences.zh: 時人重其立志。

translations.literal: Men of the time respected his firm resolve.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries respected his firm resolve.

sentences.zh: 義康欲引與日夕，湛固求外出，乃以為武陵內史，還為司徒從事中郎，遷太子中庶子，尚書吏部郎。

translations.literal: Yikang wished to draw him into daily intimacy; Zhan firmly sought to go outside and was made Interior Minister of Wuling; returning, he became Attendant of the Masters of Writing on the Secretariat, was moved to Household Vice-Steward of the Heir Apparent, and Director of Personnel in the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Yikang wished to keep him close at hand; Zhan insisted on leaving court and was made interior minister of Wuling. On his return he became secretariat attendant, then vice-steward of the heir apparent's household, then director of personnel.

sentences.zh: 隨王誕為北中郎將、南徐州刺史，以湛為長史、南東海太守，政事委之。

translations.literal: When Prince Dan of Sui was Northern Central Commandant General and Governor of Southern Xu province, he made Zhan his chief of staff and Governor of Southern Donghai, entrusting him with government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Dan of Sui was Northern Central Commandant and governor of Southern Xu, he made Zhan his chief of staff and governor of Southern Donghai, entrusting all administration to him.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十五年，徵為侍中，任以機密，領本州大中正，遷左衛將軍。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year of Yuanjia he was summoned as Palace Attendant and entrusted with confidential matters, concurrently Great Rectifier of his native province, and was moved to Left Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year of Yuanjia he was summoned as Palace Attendant and entrusted with confidential affairs, made Great Rectifier of his native province, and promoted to Left Guard General.

sentences.zh: 時改選學職，以太尉江夏王義恭領國子祭酒，湛及侍中何攸之領博士。

translations.literal: At the time academic offices were reformed; Grand Marshal Prince Yigong of Jiangxia was made Chancellor of the National University, and Zhan together with Palace Attendant He Youzhi held the post of Erudite.
translations.idiomatic: Academic offices were reformed; Grand Marshal Yigong, Prince of Jiangxia, became chancellor of the National University, while Zhan and Palace Attendant He Youzhi served as erudites.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，轉吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he was transferred to Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year he became Director of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 家甚貧約，不營財利，餉饋盈門，一無所受，無兼衣餘食。

translations.literal: His household was very poor and frugal; he did not pursue wealth; gifts filled his gate yet he accepted none; he had no spare garments or leftover food.
translations.idiomatic: His household was very poor; he sought no profit though gifts filled his gate, accepting none; he owned no spare clothes or extra food.

sentences.zh: 嘗為上所召，值浣衣，稱疾經日，衣成然後赴。

translations.literal: Once when summoned by the emperor he happened to be washing clothes; he pleaded illness for a whole day and went only after the garments were finished.
translations.idiomatic: Once when summoned by the emperor he was washing his only clothes; he pleaded illness for a day and went only after they were dry.

sentences.zh: 牛餓，馭人求草，湛良久曰：「可與飲。

translations.literal: His ox was hungry; the driver asked for fodder; after a long while Zhan said, "Give it drink."
translations.idiomatic: When his ox grew hungry the driver asked for fodder; after a long pause Zhan said, "Give it water to drink."

sentences.zh: 」在選職，頗有刻核之譏，而公平無私，不受請謁，論者以此稱焉。

translations.literal: In the selection office he drew some criticism for severity, yet he was fair and without private bias, accepting no solicitations; commentators praised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: In the selection office he drew some criticism for severity, yet he was fair and accepted no bribes; commentators praised him for this.

sentences.zh: 上大舉北代，舉朝為不可，唯湛贊成之。

translations.literal: The emperor launched a great northern campaign; the whole court held it impossible—only Zhan approved it.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor launched a great northern campaign the whole court opposed it—only Jiang Zhan supported it.

sentences.zh: 索虜至瓜步，領軍將軍劉遵考率軍出江上，以湛兼領軍，軍事處分，一以委焉。

translations.literal: When the northern barbarians reached Guabu, Army Commandant General Liu Zunkao led troops out onto the river; Zhan was made concurrent army commandant, and all military dispositions were entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Northern Wei reached Guabu, Army Commandant Liu Zunkao led troops onto the Yangtze; Zhan was made concurrent army commandant and all military decisions were entrusted to him.

sentences.zh: 虜遣使求婚，上召太子劭以下集議，眾並謂宜許，湛曰：「戎狄無信，許之無益。

translations.literal: The barbarians sent envoys to request a marriage alliance; the emperor summoned the crown prince Shao and those below to deliberate; all said it should be granted; Zhan said, "The barbarians are faithless—granting it would be of no use."
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians sent envoys seeking a marriage alliance; the emperor summoned Crown Prince Shao and the court to deliberate; all favored acceptance; Zhan said, "The barbarians are faithless—agreeing would serve no purpose."

sentences.zh: 」劭怒，謂湛曰：「今三王在厄，詎宜苟執異議。

translations.literal: Shao was angry and said to Zhan, "Now the three princes are in peril—how can you stubbornly hold to a dissenting view?"
translations.idiomatic: Shao was furious and said to Zhan, "The three princes are in peril—how can you stubbornly dissent?"

sentences.zh: 」聲色甚厲。

translations.literal: His voice and expression were very fierce.
translations.idiomatic: His tone was fierce.

sentences.zh: 坐散俱出，劭使班劍及左右推之，殆將側倒。

translations.literal: When the session broke up and all went out, Shao had his halberd guard and attendants push him, nearly toppling him sideways.
translations.idiomatic: As the meeting ended Shao had his guards and attendants shove Zhan, nearly knocking him over.

sentences.zh: 劭又謂上曰：「北伐敗辱，數州淪破，獨有斬江湛，可以謝天下。

translations.literal: Shao also said to the emperor, "The northern campaign ended in defeat and disgrace; several provinces fell—only by executing Jiang Zhan can we answer to the realm."
translations.idiomatic: Shao also told the emperor, "The northern campaign ended in defeat and several provinces were lost—only by executing Jiang Zhan can we answer to the realm."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「北伐自我意，江湛但不異耳。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "The northern campaign was my own idea; Jiang Zhan merely did not dissent—that is all."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "The northern campaign was my own decision; Jiang Zhan merely did not dissent."

sentences.zh: 」劭後燕集，未嘗命湛。

translations.literal: Afterward, at Shao's banquets and gatherings, Zhan was never invited.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Shao never invited Zhan to his banquets.

sentences.zh: 常謂上曰：「江湛佞人，不宜親也。

translations.literal: He often told the emperor, "Jiang Zhan is a flatterer and should not be kept close."
translations.idiomatic: He often told the emperor, "Jiang Zhan is a flatterer and should not be trusted."

sentences.zh: 」上乃為劭長子偉之娉湛第三女，欲以和之。

translations.literal: The emperor then betrothed Shao's eldest son Weizhi to Zhan's third daughter, wishing to reconcile them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor betrothed Shao's eldest son Weizhi to Zhan's third daughter, hoping to reconcile them.

sentences.zh: 上將廢劭，使湛具詔草。

translations.literal: When the emperor was about to depose Shao, he had Zhan draft the edict.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor prepared to depose Shao, he had Zhan draft the edict.

sentences.zh: 劭之入弑也，湛直上省，聞叫噪之聲，乃匿傍小屋中。

translations.literal: When Shao entered to commit regicide, Zhan had gone straight up to the Secretariat; hearing cries and uproar, he hid in a small room nearby.
translations.idiomatic: When Shao entered to murder the emperor, Zhan had gone to the Secretariat; hearing the uproar, he hid in a small room nearby.

sentences.zh: 劭遣收之，舍吏紿云：「不在此。

translations.literal: Shao sent men to seize him; a clerk of the office deceived them, saying, "He is not here."
translations.idiomatic: Shao sent men to seize him; an office clerk deceived them, saying he was not there.

sentences.zh: 」兵士即殺舍吏，乃得湛。

translations.literal: The soldiers at once killed the clerk and thus seized Zhan.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers killed the clerk and then seized Zhan.

sentences.zh: 湛據窗受害，意色不撓。

translations.literal: Zhan braced himself against the window as he was killed; his expression did not flinch.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan braced himself against the window as he was killed; his expression never changed.

sentences.zh: 時年四十六。

translations.literal: He was forty-six years old.
translations.idiomatic: He was forty-six.

sentences.zh: 湛五子恁、恕、憼、愻、法壽，皆見殺。

translations.literal: Zhan's five sons Ren, Shu, Cong, Xun, and Fashou were all killed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan's five sons Ren, Shu, Cong, Xun, and Fashou were all executed.

sentences.zh: 初，湛家數見怪異，未敗少日，所眠床忽有數升血。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhan's household had several times seen strange omens; a few days before his fall, several pints of blood suddenly appeared on the bed where he slept.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier strange omens had appeared in Zhan's household; a few days before his fall several pints of blood suddenly appeared on his bed.

sentences.zh: 世祖即位，追贈左光祿大夫、開府儀同三司，加散騎常侍，本官如故，諡曰忠簡公。

translations.literal: When the Shizu took the throne, he was posthumously given the offices of Left Household Grandee and Grand Master with the Golden Seal and Privileges Equal to the Three Excellencies, with the additional title of Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry; his former offices remained as before; his posthumous name was Duke of Loyal Simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu took the throne, Zhan was posthumously made Left Household Grandee with privileges equal to the Three Excellencies and Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry; his former titles were confirmed; he was posthumously styled Duke of Loyal Simplicity.

sentences.zh: 長子恁，尚太祖第九女淮陽長公主，為著作佐郎。

translations.literal: His eldest son Ren married the Eldest Princess of Huaiyang, the ninth daughter of the Taizu, and served as Assistant in the Bureau of Composition.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Ren married Eldest Princess Huaiyang, Emperor Wen's ninth daughter, and served as Assistant in the Bureau of Composition.

sentences.zh: 王僧綽，琅邪臨沂人，左光祿大夫曇首子也。

translations.literal: Wang Sengchuo was a native of Linyi in Langye commandery and the son of Tanshou, Left Household Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sengchuo came from Linyi in Langye commandery and was the son of Left Household Grandee Tanshou.

sentences.zh: 幼有大成之度，弱年眾以國器許之。

translations.literal: From childhood he had the measure of great accomplishment; in his early years all acknowledged him as material for the state.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood he showed the makings of greatness; even in youth all regarded him as a pillar of the state.

sentences.zh: 好學有理思，練悉朝典。

translations.literal: He loved learning and had principled thought; he was thoroughly versed in court regulations.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning and thought deeply; he was thoroughly versed in court regulations.

sentences.zh: 年十三，太祖引見，下拜便流涕哽咽，上亦悲不自勝。

translations.literal: At age thirteen the Taizu summoned him for an audience; as he bowed tears streamed forth and he choked with sobs; the emperor too was overcome with grief.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen Emperor Wen summoned him; as he bowed tears streamed down and he choked with sobs; the emperor too was overcome with grief.

sentences.zh: 襲封豫章縣侯，尚太祖長女東陽獻公主。

translations.literal: He inherited the enfeoffment as Marquis of Yuzhang county and married the Eldest Princess Xian of Dongyang, the eldest daughter of the Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the marquisate of Yuzhang and married Eldest Princess Xian of Dongyang, Emperor Wen's eldest daughter.

sentences.zh: 初為江夏王義恭司徒參軍，轉始興王文學，秘書丞，司徒左長史，太子中庶子。

translations.literal: He first served as Staff Officer on Prince Yigong of Jiangxia's Secretariat as Minister over the Masses, was transferred to Literary Adjunct under Prince of Shixing, Director of the Secretariat, Left Chief of Staff on the Secretariat, and Household Vice-Steward of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He began on Prince Yigong of Jiangxia's staff, then served as literary adjunct under the Prince of Shixing, director of the Secretariat, left chief of staff, and vice-steward of the heir apparent's household.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十六年，徙尚書吏部郎，參掌大選。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year of Yuanjia he was moved to Director of Personnel in the Masters of Writing and took part in overseeing the great selection.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year of Yuanjia he became Director of Personnel and took charge of major appointments.

sentences.zh: 究識流品，諳悉人物，拔才舉能，咸得其分。

translations.literal: He thoroughly understood grades of talent, was well acquainted with persons, and in raising the able and promoting talent always hit the mark.
translations.idiomatic: He thoroughly understood grades of talent, knew men well, and in promoting the able always made the right choice.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，遷侍中，任以機密。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he was moved to Palace Attendant and entrusted with confidential matters.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year he became Palace Attendant and was entrusted with confidential affairs.

sentences.zh: 僧綽沈深有局度，不以才能高人。

translations.literal: Sengchuo was deep and steady with a sense of measure; he did not set himself above others by talent.
translations.idiomatic: Sengchuo was deep and steady, with sound judgment; he did not condescend to others on account of his talent.

sentences.zh: 先是，父曇首與王華並為太祖所任，華子嗣人才既劣，位遇亦輕。

translations.literal: Earlier, his father Tanshou together with Wang Hua had both been entrusted by the Taizu; Hua's son Si was inferior in talent and his rank and favor were likewise slight.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tanshou and Wang Hua had both been trusted by Emperor Wen; Hua's son Si was inferior in talent and held a far lower position.

sentences.zh: 僧綽嘗謂中書侍郎蔡興宗曰：「弟名位應與新建齊，超至今日，蓋由姻戚所致也。

translations.literal: Sengchuo once said to Vice Director of the Central Secretariat Cai Xingzong: "Brother, in name and rank you ought to stand level with the Marquis of Xinjian; that you have risen to your present height is surely due to marriage connections."
translations.idiomatic: Sengchuo once told Vice Director Cai Xingzong: "Brother, your rank ought to match the Marquis of Xinjian's; you have risen higher chiefly through marriage ties."

sentences.zh: 」新建者，嗣之封也。

translations.literal: Xinjian was Si's enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Xinjian was Wang Si's title.

sentences.zh: 及為侍中，時年二十九。

translations.literal: When he became Palace Attendant he was twenty-nine years old.
translations.idiomatic: When he became Palace Attendant he was twenty-nine.

sentences.zh: 始興王浚嘗問其年，僧綽自嫌蚤達，逡巡良久乃答，其謙虛自退若此。

translations.literal: Prince Jun of Shixing once asked his age; Sengchuo, ashamed of his early advancement, hesitated a long while before answering—such was his modest self-restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jun of Shixing once asked his age; ashamed of his early advancement, Sengchuo hesitated a long while before answering—such was his modesty.

sentences.zh: 元嘉末，太祖頗以後事為念，以其年少，方欲大相付託，朝政小大，皆與參焉。

translations.literal: At the end of Yuanjia the Taizu thought much of affairs after his death; though Sengchuo was young, he was about to entrust him with great responsibility; in court affairs great and small he was all consulted.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Yuanjia Emperor Wen thought much of the succession; though Sengchuo was young, he intended to entrust him with great responsibility and consulted him on all matters of state.

sentences.zh: 從兄徽，清介士也，懼其太盛，勸令損抑。

translations.literal: His cousin Hui was a man of pure integrity; fearing that Sengchuo's eminence was too great, he urged him to restrain and lower himself.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Hui, a man of pure integrity, fearing his eminence had grown excessive, urged him to restrain himself.

sentences.zh: 僧綽乃求吳郡及廣州，上並不許。

translations.literal: Sengchuo then requested Wu commandery and Guang province; the emperor permitted neither.
translations.idiomatic: Sengchuo then asked for posts in Wu commandery and Guang province; the emperor refused both.

sentences.zh: 會二凶巫蠱事泄，上獨先召僧綽具言之。

translations.literal: When the witchcraft affair of the two villains was exposed, the emperor first summoned Sengchuo alone and told him the full account.
translations.idiomatic: When the witchcraft plot of the two princes was exposed, the emperor summoned Sengchuo alone and told him everything.

sentences.zh: 及將廢立，使尋求前朝舊典。

translations.literal: When he was about to depose and establish an heir, he had him search out the old precedents of former dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: When he prepared to depose the heir and name another, he had Sengchuo search out precedents from earlier dynasties.

sentences.zh: 劭於東宮夜饗將士，僧綽密以啟聞，上又令撰漢魏以來廢諸王故事。

translations.literal: When Shao feasted his officers at night in the Eastern Palace, Sengchuo secretly reported it; the emperor also ordered him to compile precedents since Han and Wei for deposing princes.
translations.idiomatic: When Shao feasted his officers at night in the Eastern Palace, Sengchuo secretly informed the emperor, who also ordered him to compile precedents since Han and Wei for deposing princes.

sentences.zh: 撰畢，送與江湛、徐湛之。

translations.literal: When the compilation was finished, it was sent to Jiang Zhan and Xu Zhanzhi.
translations.idiomatic: When the compilation was finished it was sent to Jiang Zhan and Xu Zhanzhi.

sentences.zh: 湛之欲立隨王誕，江湛欲立南平王鑠，太祖欲立建平王宏，議久不決。

translations.literal: Zhanzhi wished to establish Prince Dan of Sui; Jiang Zhan wished to establish Prince Shuo of Nanping; the Taizu wished to establish Prince Hong of Jianping; deliberation long went unresolved.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zhanzhi favored Prince Dan of Sui; Jiang Zhan favored Prince Shuo of Nanping; Emperor Wen favored Prince Hong of Jianping; deliberation dragged on without resolution.

sentences.zh: 延妃即湛之女，鑠妃即湛妹。

translations.literal: Dan's consort was Zhanzhi's daughter; Shuo's consort was Zhanzhi's younger sister.
translations.idiomatic: Dan's consort was Xu Zhanzhi's daughter; Shuo's consort was his sister.

sentences.zh: 太祖謂僧綽曰：「諸人各為身計，便無與國家同憂者。

translations.literal: The Taizu said to Sengchuo: "Each of these men schemes for himself; there is none who shares the state's concern."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen told Sengchuo: "Each of them schemes for himself; none shares the state's concern."

sentences.zh: 」僧綽曰：「建立之事，仰由聖懷。

translations.literal: Sengchuo said: "The matter of establishing an heir rests with Your sacred intent.
translations.idiomatic: Sengchuo replied: "The choice of heir rests with Your Majesty alone.

sentences.zh: 臣謂唯宜速斷，不可稽緩。

translations.literal: Your subject holds that you should decide swiftly and must not delay.
translations.idiomatic: I believe you should decide swiftly and not delay.

sentences.zh: 當斷不斷，反受其亂。

translations.literal: When one ought to decide and does not, one suffers disorder in return.
translations.idiomatic: He who ought to decide and does not will suffer disorder in return.

sentences.zh: 願以義割恩，略小不忍。

translations.literal: I pray that you may sever affection by righteousness and set aside small reluctance to act.
translations.idiomatic: I pray that you will let righteousness override affection and set aside small reluctance to act.

sentences.zh: 不爾，便應坦懷如初，無煩疑論。

translations.literal: If not, you should open your heart as at first and have no need for suspicious talk.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise you should be open-hearted as before and have no need for suspicious deliberation.

sentences.zh: 淮南云：'以石投水，吳越之善沒取之。

translations.literal: The Huainanzi says: 'Cast a stone into water and the expert divers of Wu and Yue will fetch it out.'
translations.idiomatic: The Huainanzi says: 'Cast a stone into water and the expert divers of Wu and Yue will fetch it out.'

sentences.zh: '事機雖密，易致宣廣，不可使難生慮表，取笑千載。

translations.literal: Though the affair is secret, it is easy for it to spread abroad; you must not let trouble arise in men's minds and become a laughingstock for a thousand years.'
translations.idiomatic: Though the affair is secret, it can easily leak abroad; you must not let suspicion arise and become a laughingstock for ages.'

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「卿可謂能斷大事。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "You may be said to be able to decide great affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You may be said to know how to decide great affairs.

sentences.zh: 此事重，不可不殷勤三思。

translations.literal: This matter is weighty and cannot but be thrice considered with earnest care.
translations.idiomatic: This matter is weighty and must be considered again and again with the utmost care.

sentences.zh: 且庶人始亡，人將謂我無復慈愛之道。

translations.literal: Moreover, the commoner has only just died; men will say I no longer have the way of loving-kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, my son has only just died; men will say I no longer know fatherly love.

sentences.zh: 」僧綽曰：「臣恐千載之後，言陛下唯能裁弟，不能裁兒。

translations.literal: Sengchuo said, "Your subject fears that a thousand years hence men will say Your Majesty could only judge younger brothers, not sons."
translations.idiomatic: Sengchuo replied, "I fear that ages hence men will say Your Majesty could judge younger brothers but not his own son."

sentences.zh: 」上默然。

translations.literal: The emperor was silent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor fell silent.

sentences.zh: 江湛同侍坐，出閣，謂僧綽曰：「卿向言，將不大傷切直。

translations.literal: Jiang Zhan had been sitting in attendance with him; leaving the pavilion he said to Sengchuo, "What you just said will wound him rather deeply with its bluntness."
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Zhan had been in attendance; leaving the pavilion he told Sengchuo, "What you just said was rather blunt and will wound him deeply."

sentences.zh: 」僧綽曰：「弟亦恨君不直。」

translations.literal: Sengchuo said, "Brother, I too regret that you were not blunt."
translations.idiomatic: Sengchuo replied, "Brother, I too regret that you were not blunt enough."

sentences.zh: 及劭弑逆，江湛在尚書上省，聞變，歎曰：「不用僧綽言，以至於此。

translations.literal: When Shao committed regicide, Jiang Zhan was in the upper offices of the Masters of Writing; hearing the upheaval, he sighed and said, "Had we not taken Sengchuo's counsel, it would not have come to this."
translations.idiomatic: When Shao murdered the emperor, Jiang Zhan was at the Masters of Writing offices; hearing the news he sighed, "Had we heeded Sengchuo's counsel, it would not have come to this."

sentences.zh: 」劭既立，轉為吏部尚書，委以事任，事在《二凶傳》。

translations.literal: After Shao had usurped the throne, Sengchuo was transferred to Director of the Ministry of Personnel and entrusted with affairs of office; the matter is recorded in the 《Biography of the Two Villains》.
translations.idiomatic: After Shao usurped the throne, Sengchuo was made Director of Personnel and entrusted with affairs of state; the account is in the 《Biography of the Two Villains》.

sentences.zh: 頃之，劭料檢太祖巾箱及江湛家書疏，得僧綽所啟饗士並廢諸王事，乃收害焉，時年三十一。

translations.literal: Before long, Shao examined the Taizu's scarf-box and the letters and documents in Jiang Zhan's household; he found Sengchuo's reports on feasting the officers and deposing the princes, and thereupon seized and killed him; he was thirty-one years old.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Shao searched the emperor's private chest and Jiang Zhan's papers; finding Sengchuo's reports on the feast for officers and the plan to depose the princes, he had him seized and killed; Sengchuo was thirty-one.

sentences.zh: 因此陷北第諸王侯，以為與僧綽有異志，並殺僧綽門客太學博士賈匪之、奉朝請司馬文穎、建平國常侍司馬仲秀等。

translations.literal: On this pretext he implicated the princes and marquises of the Northern Residence, holding that they shared Sengchuo's disloyal intent; he also killed Sengchuo's clients Jia Feizhi, Erudite of the National University, Sima Wenying, Court Attendant, Sima Zhongxiu, Regular Attendant of the Principality of Jianping, and others.
translations.idiomatic: On this pretext he implicated the princes of the Northern Residence, claiming they shared Sengchuo's disloyal intent; he also executed Sengchuo's clients Jia Feizhi, Erudite of the National University, court attendant Sima Wenying, regular attendant Sima Zhongxiu of Jianping, and others.

sentences.zh: 世祖即位，追贈散騎常侍、金紫光祿大夫，諡曰湣侯。

translations.literal: When the Shizu took the throne, he was posthumously given the titles of Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Household Grandee with the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon; his posthumous name was Marquis of Lamentation.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu took the throne, Sengchuo was posthumously made Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Household Grandee with the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon; he was posthumously styled Marquis of Lamentation.

sentences.zh: 初，太社西空地一區，吳時丁奉宅，孫晧流徙其家。

translations.literal: Earlier, a vacant plot west of the Grand Altar of Soil and Grain had been the residence of Ding Feng in Wu times; Sun Hao exiled his household from it.
translations.idiomatic: A vacant plot west of the Grand Altar of Soil and Grain had been Ding Feng's residence in Wu times; Sun Hao exiled his household from it.

sentences.zh: 江左初為周顗、蘇峻宅，其後為袁悅宅，又為章武王司馬秀宅，皆以凶終。

translations.literal: In the early years south of the Yangtze it was the residence of Zhou Yi and Su Jun; afterward it was Yuan Yue's residence, then Prince of Zhangwu Sima Xiu's residence—all ended in violent death.
translations.idiomatic: In the early years south of the Yangtze it had been the home of Zhou Yi and Su Jun; later of Yuan Yue, then of Prince Zhangwu Sima Xiu—all met violent ends.

sentences.zh: 後給臧燾，亦頗遇喪禍，故世稱為凶地。

translations.literal: Later it was given to Zang Tao, who also met with considerable bereavement and disaster; therefore the age called it an ill-omened place.
translations.idiomatic: Later it was given to Zang Tao, who also suffered bereavement and disaster; the age therefore called it an ill-omened place.

sentences.zh: 僧綽常以正達自居，謂宅無吉凶，請以為第。

translations.literal: Sengchuo always set himself up as a man of upright attainment, held that dwellings had no luck or ill luck, and asked to take it as his residence.
translations.idiomatic: Sengchuo, holding himself a man of upright character, maintained that dwellings had no luck or ill luck and asked to take it as his residence.

sentences.zh: 始就造築，未及居而敗。

translations.literal: He had just begun construction and, before he could dwell there, met his downfall.
translations.idiomatic: He had just begun building when, before he could move in, he met his downfall.

sentences.zh: 子儉嗣，升明末，為齊國尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: His son Jian succeeded; at the end of the Shengming era he served as Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing in the State of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jian succeeded; at the end of the Shengming era he was Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing in Qi.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：甚矣，宋氏之家難也，仇釁所鐘，親地兼極，雖復傾天滅道，跡非嫌路，而災隙內兆，邪蠱外興，天性既離，愛敬同盡，探雀請熊，非無前釁，猜防之道，有未足乎。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: How great were the domestic calamities of the house of Song! Enmity and strife converged upon them; kinship reached its extreme. Though they overturned Heaven and extinguished the Way, their tracks were not those of mere suspicion—yet disaster sprouted within, wicked witchcraft arose without; natural affection was already severed, love and reverence alike exhausted. To take a sparrow and ask for a bear—was there no prior omen? Were the ways of suspicion and guard not yet sufficient?
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: How severe were the Liu Song's domestic calamities! Enmity converged upon them as kinship reached its breaking point. Though they overturned Heaven and extinguished the Way, their course was not mere suspicion—yet disaster sprouted within while witchcraft arose without; natural affection was severed and love and reverence alike exhausted. To take a sparrow and demand a bear—had there been no prior warning? Were suspicion and precaution not yet enough?

sentences.zh: 世祖弱年輕躁，夙無朝寵，累任邊外，未嘗居中。

translations.literal: The Shizu in his youth was frivolous and impetuous; from of old he had no favor at court; he was repeatedly posted to the border regions and never held the center.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jun in his youth was frivolous and impetuous; he had never enjoyed favor at court; repeatedly posted to the frontiers, he had never held power at the center.

sentences.zh: 當璧之重，將由愛立，臣主回疑，事無蚤斷。

translations.literal: The weight of holding the jade disk was to be settled by affection; ruler and ministers wavered in doubt; the affair had no early resolution.
translations.idiomatic: The choice of heir was to be settled by affection; ruler and ministers wavered; the matter was never decided in time.

sentences.zh: 若使守器以長，命不待賢，則密禍自銷，危機可免。

translations.literal: If the heir had been kept on the vessel by seniority and the mandate had not awaited the worthy, then hidden calamity would have dissolved of itself and the crisis could have been avoided.
translations.idiomatic: If the heir had been kept by seniority and the throne had not awaited the worthy, hidden calamity would have dissolved and crisis been avoided.

sentences.zh: 聖哲之訓，豈欺我哉！

translations.literal: The teachings of the sages—can they deceive us!
translations.idiomatic: Can the teachings of the sages deceive us!

sentences.zh: 昔山濤舉羊祜為太子太傅，蓋欲以後事委之，而羊公短世。

translations.literal: Formerly Shan Tao recommended Yang Hu as Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, intending to entrust later affairs to him, but Lord Yang died young.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Shan Tao recommended Yang Hu as Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, intending to entrust the succession to him, but Yang Hu died young.

sentences.zh: 僧綽綢繆主心，將任以國重，而宮車晏駕。

translations.literal: Sengchuo had bound the ruler's heart and was about to be entrusted with the weight of the state, but the imperial carriage halted at dusk.
translations.idiomatic: Sengchuo had won the emperor's trust and was about to be entrusted with the weight of state, but the emperor died before he could take office.

sentences.zh: 二臣並以道德謙沖，名高兩代。

translations.literal: Both ministers were alike in moral virtue and modest humility, their fame high across two generations.
translations.idiomatic: Both men were alike in moral virtue and modest humility, renowned across two generations.

sentences.zh: 胙未中年，功謝成日，惜矣哉！

translations.literal: Their blessings had not reached midlife; their merit departed before its day—how regrettable!
translations.idiomatic: They had not reached midlife; their merit departed before its day—how regrettable!
